title: Dictionary Secrets and Tips
summary: Find Spanish words efficiently and understand meanings, abbreviations and guide words.
keyIdeas: Words follow alphabetical order. When initial letters match, compare the next letters.
Noun headwords are usually singular, keeping their gender. Two-ending adjectives usually use masculine singular headwords; verbs use infinitives.
A numbered meaning is an «acepción». Guide words show the first and last headwords on a page.

basicKnowledge: D. Reflexión sobre la lengua y sus usos en el marco de propuestas de producción y comprensión de textos orales, escritos o multimodales

activities.prompt: Hugo sorts vocabulary cards. Put these Spanish words in dictionary order.
activities.explanation: All begin with b. Compare their second letters: a, o, r, u.

activities.prompt: Lucía finds «escribíamos» in a novel. Which headword should she look up?
activities.explanation: The infinitive headword for this verb form is «escribir».

activities.prompt: A school dictionary page has guide words «farola» and «fiesta». «Felino» belongs in that alphabetical range.
Match each Spanish dictionary abbreviation with its meaning.
activities.explanation: Abbreviations give information about a word's grammar or related meanings.

activities.prompt: For this activity, use usual headword forms: singular nouns, masculine singular adjectives and infinitive verbs. Sort by whether the form needs changing.
activities.explanation: «Árbol», «dormir» and «sol» already have these forms. Change «cantábamos» to «cantar», «altas» to «alto» and «pequeñitos» to singular «pequeñito». Some digital dictionaries also accept inflected searches.

activities.prompt: Complete the Spanish definition with the correct term.
activities.explanation: An «acepción» is one of a word's meanings in a dictionary entry.

activities.prompt: Adrián explains dictionary headwords. Which statement is INCORRECT?
activities.explanation: For the adjective «listas», use the headword «listo», rather than treating the feminine plural as the usual headword.
activities.hint: Think about the headword form of a two-ending adjective.
options: Words with the same first letter are ordered by their next letters.
For the adjective «listas», the usual dictionary headword is «listas» in the plural.
To find the meaning of «comiste», look up «comer».

activities.prompt: Read the Spanish classroom investigation and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: The story shows how dictionary editions and their contents can differ as language changes.
activities.title: El misterio del tomo gastado
activities.text:
Durante la clase de Lengua, Omar y Nerea encontraron un diccionario ilustrado antiguo en la biblioteca. Al abrirlo por la letra C, vieron las palabras guía «Calamar - Calina». Entre ellas descubrieron palabras poco usadas y dibujos de animales marinos.

Nerea buscó «videollamada», pero no aparecía en ese ejemplar. Omar recordó que un diccionario no recoge todas las palabras de la lengua y que sus ediciones se actualizan. Consultaron un diccionario digital reciente y encontraron la palabra y su significado. Compararon ambas obras: la antigua conservaba vocabulario de otra época y la actual incorporaba usos nuevos. Comprendieron que la lengua cambia y que conviene elegir un diccionario adecuado para cada consulta.

questions.prompt: What did they do when «videollamada» was missing from that copy?
options: They consulted a recent digital dictionary.
They decided the word did not exist.
They tore pages out of the old dictionary.
questions.explanation: The text says they found the word and its meaning in a recent digital dictionary.

questions.prompt: With guide words «Calamar - Calina», which word could be on the same page?
questions.explanation: «Calambre» comes between «calamar» and «calina». «Cacao» is earlier and «calor» later.

questions.prompt: What do Omar and Nerea conclude about language?
questions.explanation: Language changes with society, and dictionaries are updated to record changing usage.
options: Old dictionaries are better and more accurate than modern ones.
Language and dictionaries evolve with society.
There is no need to use a dictionary if we know modern words.

activities.prompt: Which series is in strict Spanish alphabetical order?
activities.explanation: Compare successive letters: «desac...» comes before «desan...», then «desc...» and «desf...». Accent marks do not change this ordering.
activities.hint: Compare one letter at a time.
